stories.title: Trump says UK-US relations better with Burnham than Starmer after first face-to-face meeting
stories.summary: Donald Trump declared Andy Burnham 'a man he can do business with' after their first in-person meeting at the UN General Assembly in New York, saying UK-US relations have improved since Burnham replaced Keir Starmer as PM. Some testy topics arose including Iran and West Bank sanctions.

stories.title: UK to fight Russian disinformation and push new global AI standards, Burnham says
stories.summary: In his UN General Assembly speech, Burnham accused Russia of running a disinformation campaign and argued the UK is 'uniquely placed' to lead international AI governance. He also announced plans to push new global AI safety standards.

stories.title: England's mayors should face greater scrutiny as powers expand, thinktank says
stories.summary: A thinktank report warns that as Burnham places the transfer of power outside Whitehall at the heart of his government — including via No 10 North in Manchester — greater scrutiny mechanisms for mayors are urgently needed to maintain democratic accountability.

topics.name: Burnham Gov Intelligence
topics.description: Procurement, tech/AI, spending, vendor & priority signals

stories.title: 🤖 Burnham pushes global AI governance framework at UNGA
stories.summary: PM Burnham told the UN General Assembly that Britain is uniquely placed to mediate between US and Chinese AI approaches, pushing for international guardrails. The UK government is positioning itself as the neutral arbiter of global AI standards.

stories.title: 🤖 DSIT watchdog grills government over 'serious concerns on budgets and delivery' after dissolution
stories.summary: The DSIT (Dept for Science, Innovation and Technology) watchdog has raised serious concerns about budgets and delivery performance following the department's dissolution. This signals potential funding and delivery risk across the UK government's digital and tech portfolio.

stories.title: 🤖 Committee chair warns over AI wealth giveaway to tech firms
stories.summary: A parliamentary committee chair has warned the government against an AI 'wealth giveaway', flagging risks that public sector AI contracts disproportionately benefit large tech firms without sufficient return to the public purse.

stories.title: 🏗️ Version 1 wins £52m HM Land Registry data delivery deal
stories.summary: Version 1 has won a £52m contract with HM Land Registry to lead data delivery and digital transformation. The contract covers design and build of a prototype environment to reshape how land and property data in England and Wales is accessed, with work already underway.

stories.title: 🤖 Gateway makes MHCLG AI usage safer with single secure access route
stories.summary: A new gateway solution creates a single, secure route for product and delivery teams within the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG) to access approved AI tools, reducing shadow AI risk.

topics.name: Parliament
topics.description: House of Commons, Lords, PMQs & legislation

stories.title: MPs call for protection of OBR role and longer-term fiscal thinking
stories.summary: The Treasury Committee has published a report calling for stronger protection of the Office for Budget Responsibility's independence and urging the government to adopt longer-term fiscal planning. Professor Jonathan Haskel has been approved as the new OBR Chair.

stories.title: House of Commons Fracking Ban Debate aired
stories.summary: The House of Commons held a debate on the merits of a full ban on fracking, reflecting ongoing parliamentary scrutiny of energy policy under the Burnham government. The debate was broadcast on BBC Parliament.

stories.title: Burnham warns new EU industry rules would damage UK
stories.summary: PM Burnham warned that new EU proposals designed to protect European industry from Chinese competition — by giving EU-based companies priority for public contracts and subsidies — would significantly damage UK businesses and trade.

stories.title: October tax rises 'inevitable' as Labour borrowing hits second-highest August on record
stories.summary: Government borrowing in August hit its second-highest level on record for that month, fuelling warnings that tax rises expected in October are now unavoidable. Labour faces growing pressure on its fiscal plans.

stories.title: Trade unions, MPs and donors urge Burnham to revisit party funding rules
stories.summary: A coalition of trade unions, Labour MPs and major donors are pressing Burnham to revisit party funding rules, amid concerns that Reform UK's record donations are shifting the political landscape. The TUC chief has warned the 'super-rich' threaten democracy.

stories.title: Badenoch instructs lawyers to challenge government over Wandsworth Council's 94% council tax hike
stories.summary: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has instructed lawyers to legally challenge the government after a Tory-run Wandsworth Council was forced into a 94% council tax increase, blaming central government funding decisions. The move escalates Tory-government tensions.

stories.title: Burnham criticises Badenoch for excluding those who care about human rights or climate action
stories.summary: PM Burnham publicly attacked Kemi Badenoch at UNGA, accusing her of 'excluding from the Conservative party anyone who cares about human rights or climate action'. Badenoch also faced criticism from Burnham for not responding forcefully enough to Russia's disinformation campaign.

stories.title: Ed Davey promises £17bn income tax cut if Lib Dems are elected
stories.summary: In his keynote conference speech, Ed Davey pledged a £17 billion income tax cut and promised that the UK would rejoin the EU single market if the Lib Dems came to power. The announcement was the centrepiece of a buoyant party conference.

stories.title: Lib Dems leave conference buoyed by Davey's message despite internal tensions
stories.summary: The Liberal Democrat conference ended on an upbeat note after Davey's speech rallied the party, despite some MPs raising concerns in private about ambition and direction. Davey's strategy focuses on winning over disaffected Conservative voters.

stories.title: Davey says far right in Britain now better funded and supported than ever
stories.summary: Lib Dem leader Ed Davey warned at his party conference that the far right in Britain is now 'better funded and supported than in the past', calling for a unified liberal democratic response to counter the rise of populism.

stories.title: Thinktank linked to Reform UK calls for abolition of state pension
stories.summary: A thinktank with links to Reform UK has published a paper calling for the abolition of the state pension, igniting political controversy. The move comes amid broader financial scandals in the party, including a foreign donation investigation.

stories.title: Reform UK-led council ends support for Show Racism the Red Card
stories.summary: A Sunderland council led by Reform UK has ended its support for the anti-racism educational organisation Show Racism the Red Card, a decision that has provoked significant backlash and highlighted concerns about the direction of Reform-controlled councils.

stories.title: Laura Anne Jones elected Reform's deputy Welsh leader
stories.summary: Laura Anne Jones has been elected as the new deputy leader of Reform UK in Wales, following party turmoil that included the arrest of the previous Welsh leader and an investigation into breaches of foreign donation rules.

stories.title: SNP depute leader 'very confident' of winning second independence vote
stories.summary: The SNP's depute leader has said he wants a fresh vote on Scottish independence 'as soon as possible', stating he is 'very confident' the public will vote Yes. This follows the SNP falling short of an outright majority but securing a large pro-independence coalition with the Greens at Holyrood.

stories.title: Reform MSPs walk out of Holyrood independence debate
stories.summary: Reform UK MSPs staged a walkout during a Holyrood debate on Scottish independence, protesting the SNP and Greens' push for a second referendum. The pro-independence parties hold the largest majority in devolution history with 73 combined MSPs.

stories.title: Scotland has right to decide its constitutional future, new Scottish Labour leader says
stories.summary: The newly elected Scottish Labour leader has declared that Scotland has the right to decide its own constitutional future, a notable shift in tone that signals a more open approach to the independence question than previous Scottish Labour positions.

stories.title: Keep Britain Working: government publishes national growth opportunity review
stories.summary: The government has published the September 2026 update to its 'Keep Britain Working' review, positioning it as a national growth opportunity. The review focuses on workforce participation, economic inactivity, and public sector employment strategies.

stories.title: Digital ID officials 'being redeployed to other government priorities'
stories.summary: Officials working on the UK's digital identity programme have been redeployed to other government priorities, raising questions about the future timeline of the digital ID rollout. The move signals a potential pause or deprioritisation of the digital ID agenda.

topics.name: Elections & By-elections
topics.description: Upcoming or recent elections, polls & results

stories.title: By-election bill revealed after rivals' cost row — Reform's Katie Groom wins seat
stories.summary: Reform UK's Katie Groom has won a local by-election, with Reform taking 41 of 54 seats in the authority. A new by-election bill has been revealed following a dispute over costs among rivals, potentially affecting future by-election processes.

stories.title: Isle of Man general election set for 24 September
stories.summary: The Isle of Man general election takes place on Thursday 24 September, with 24 members of the House of Keys to be elected. Voters go to the polls every five years in the island's parliament.

stories.title: Lords Committee criticises Home Secretary's power to change immigration rules without parliamentary scrutiny
stories.summary: A House of Lords committee has raised concerns over the Home Secretary's power to alter immigration rules via secondary legislation with minimal parliamentary oversight. The committee is calling for greater scrutiny of such executive powers.

stories.title: MPs call for protection of OBR independence and longer-term fiscal thinking
stories.summary: The Treasury Select Committee has urged both Houses to support stronger protections for the Office for Budget Responsibility's independence, citing concerns about short-term political pressures on fiscal forecasting.
